claims.text: Minor Hf and Ta additions will improve the mechanical performance of the refractory HEA under high-temperature irradiation conditions.
Minor Hf and Ta additions will preserve the alloy's thermal stability.
Minor Hf and Ta additions will preserve the alloy's irradiation stability.
Adding Hf and Ta increases lattice distortion or lattice strain in the HEA.
Adding Hf and Ta produces a higher density of recombination sites for irradiation-induced point defects.
The increased lattice strain impedes dislocation motion.
The proposed modification improves vacancy-interstitial recombination rates.
Severe lattice distortion restricts the formation and growth of irradiation-induced defect clusters.
The Hf/Ta modification reduces irradiation-induced blister formation.
The Hf/Ta-modified alloy will have higher hardness than the unmodified alloy under equivalent conditions.
The Hf/Ta-modified alloy will have higher yield strength than the unmodified alloy under equivalent conditions.
The Hf/Ta-modified alloy will develop smaller helium bubbles than the unmodified alloy under equivalent irradiation.
The Hf/Ta-modified alloy will have lower dislocation densities in critical irradiated regions.
Keeping Hf and Ta below approximately 5 atomic percent avoids phase instability or undesired segregation.
The proposed benefit applies during combined high-temperature exposure and high-flux Kr and He ion irradiation.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts reduced bubble aggregation and smaller He bubbles as beneficial, whereas the cited record reports large and increasingly dense He bubbles in Hf1Ta HEA and identifies their interaction with dislocations as the main cause of irradiation hardening.
